key_insight: A mixture-of-experts model learns flow corrections from data-assimilated simulations, achieving accuracy close to assimilation without requiring experimental inputs during deployment.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a route to more accurate axial-compressor flow predictions by augmenting baseline RANS with learned forcing terms.
method: Fuse experimental PIV data with steady fixed-grid RANS and unsteady moving-grid hybrid RANS/LES using MFEnKF.
Train neural networks on the enriched database to map local velocity, velocity gradients and turbulent viscosity to forcing terms.
Use a mixture of experts to classify flow regions and combine trained models.
evidence_signal: Against experimental data, the mixture-of-experts predictions show systematically lower discrepancies than baseline RANS and accuracy very similar to MFEnKF.
watch_item: Individual learned models can produce localized errors near blade tips that exceed baseline RANS errors, making region-aware model selection important.
paper_title: Assisted Turbulence Modeling via Data Assimilation and Machine Learning for Turbomachinery Flows
